positive.query: We close the books on business day 12 and it keeps slipping. Build a month-end close calendar with owners and a close checklist for our three-person finance team.
Set up balance-sheet account reconciliations and a flux analysis with our thresholds of 25,000 and 10% before we lock March.
How do we shorten our close from BD+10 to BD+6? Tell us what to move pre-close and what to automate.

nearMiss.query: Marketing spend came in 18% over budget last quarter. Write a short explanation of the variance for the board.
Build a 13-week cash flow forecast so we can see if we breach the minimum cash covenant in May.
Is this multi-year licence with bundled implementation services one performance obligation or two under ASC 606? Give us the accounting conclusion.

holdout.query: Write our journal entry support and review standard and a sign-off and lock procedure for the monthly close.

scenarios.task: A hypothetical single-entity subscription software company with 60 employees, a controller, and two accountants closes on BD+11. It uses a GL, a billing system, and an outsourced payroll provider, and has deferred revenue, prepaid software, and a small fixed asset base. The owner wants a close calendar, the core checklist, a balance-sheet reconciliation template, a flux method using thresholds of 20,000 and 10%, and a plan to reach BD+7. No revenue policy document was supplied.
scenarios.baselineFailure: The baseline produces a generic checklist without business-day sequencing, owners, reviewer separation, a deferred revenue roll-forward, or a flux explanation standard, and silently invents a revenue policy or materiality level.

scenarios.task: Using hypothetical figures, review this flux with thresholds of 10,000 and 10% applied as a both-tests rule: software expense 50,000 prior month and 62,000 current; rent 100,000 and 108,000; travel 2,000 and 5,000; payroll 400,000 and 460,000 with headcount unchanged. Say which lines need explanations, what evidence to request, and what an acceptable explanation must contain.
scenarios.baselineFailure: The baseline miscalculates percentages, applies the threshold inconsistently, and accepts explanations such as timing or higher activity without cause, quantification, and evidence.
